newsitem.title: INDIA: Institution buying boosts Delhi shares by 1.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Institution buying boosts Delhi shares by 1.3 pct.

text.p: Sizeable purchases by domestic financial institutions and sustained buying by foreign financial institutions pushed Delhi share prices to a sharply higher close on Friday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 10.90 points, or 1. 3 percent, higher at 849.04.
"Heavy buying by the Unit Trust of India has fuelled the present rally in share prices," said one broker.
Traders said institutional buying also inspired small investors to make fresh stakes.

"Speculators have been building large positions in highly active shares for the last few sessions which has mainly revived bullish conditions on the market," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.

ITC surged 9.25 rupees to 529.85 on institutional buying following rumours that Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc, a major shareholder in ITC, might enhance its controlling stake in the company, brokers said.
B.A.T holds a 31.7 percent stake in ITC.

Reliance Industries, after trading in alternate bouts of buying and selling, closed 3.90 rupees lower at 321.00 on profit-taking, brokers said. It had rallied strongly earlier in the week on rumours of an impending bonus issue.
Hindustan Lever ended 7.00 rupees higher at 1,295.00.
TELCO spurted 19.00 rupees, or 4.69 percent, to 425.50.
Larsen and Toubro ended 1.60 rupees higher at 237.50.
